newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Light distillate draw seen in API data.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Light distillate draw seen in API data.

text.p: Tuesday evening's oil inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) was expected to show a minor draw in distillate stocks as a seasonal tendency for stock declines was expected to be offset somewhat by slack demand.

"We didn't get the onslaught of the cold weather in the East Coast until much later in the week, so it's hard to say how much of a draw we will have," said Amoco Corp chief economist Theodore Eck. An average of trader estimates pegged the distillate draw at 1.0 million barrels.
Estimates for distillate stocks, which are comprised of heating oil and diesel, ranged from unchanged to off 2.5 million barrels. The data is for the week ended January 10.
Crude stocks are expected to show a large build after declining 9.5 million barrels for the week ended January 3.

"Last week we had a draw down by refiners mainly for tax purposes, but this week we are going to see imports show up that didn't make it in last week," said Jim Ritterbusch, a trader with Sweeney Oil. Trader estimates ranged from up 500,000 barrels to up five million barrels.

The consensus pegged the crude build at 2.3 million barrels. Bad driving weather and a planned build in refined product stocks ahead of refinery turnarounds are supposed to create a significant build in gasoline stocks as well.
"Refiners tend to stock up on products ahead of turnarounds, so they won't get caught short during maintenance," said an analyst with a large refiner.

Gasoline stocks were seen building anywhere from 800,000 barrels to four million barrels. Several large refiners, including Mobil and Exxon, deferred maintenance until January to build depleted distillate stocks ahead of winter.
Consequently, dealers expected refinery utilization rates to drop 0.5 to 1.0 percentage point from 92.3 percent.

Though analysts said the cold snap in the "heating oil belt" of the U.S. Northeast hit the region too late to be included in this week's data, some said refineries may have already stocked up enough distillate before going into turnaround, tempering a build.

"We have recently seen large distillate builds, so these refiners may have enough," said one dealer. Moreover, the seasonal trend strongly favors a decline. Last year at this time, distillate stocks fell by almost six million barrels.
In January, refiners start shifting their output slate away from distillate and toward gasoline ahead of the summer driving season, resulting in declines in distillate stocks.
